missions.title: Strong Mind, Smart Moves
missions.story: The town is preparing for Friendly Games Day. The learners must help classmates manage worries, prepare a safe play area, and solve a team challenge using kindness and movement skills.
missions.focus: Healthy coping and assertiveness; Grade 5 striking/fielding movement concepts, positioning and fair play.

finalChallenge.title: Friendly Games Day Finale
finalChallenge.description: Friendly Games Day finale: inspect the play area, choose safe field positions and select a respectful response to a bullying scenario; demonstrate a basic skill with teacher observation when feasible.

steps.prompt: Friendly Games Day Finale: sort the field inspection items into Safe Play Area vs Hazard to Clear.
items: Smooth open grass cleared of stones and glass
Fallen broken tree branch across the running lane
Well-placed safety boundary cones
Deep slippery puddle in the striking zone
steps.success: Play area inspected and secured!

steps.prompt: Choose the most respectful and assertive response when resolving a game dispute:
items: Refuse to continue and take the ball home
Speak calmly: 'Let's check the rules together and replay the point fairly.'
Insult the player who made a mistake
steps.success: Mission 1 complete! You earned the Kindness and Movement Badge!

checkpoints.title: Calm Garden
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Calm Garden. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Stress may make a person feel nervous, worried or tense. Healthy responses include slow breathing, preparation, positive self-talk and asking a trusted adult for help. Assertive speech is clear and respectful rather than hurtful.

miniGame.name: Emotion Cards
miniGame.instructions: Sort four scenario cards into helpful coping responses and unhelpful reactions.

steps.prompt: Emotion Cards: sort each response into Helpful Coping vs Unhelpful Reaction.
items: Taking slow deep breaths and reviewing notes
Shouting at classmates in frustration
Using positive self-talk: 'I can practice and improve'
Hiding all materials and quitting
steps.success: Great job! You know how to choose healthy coping responses.

questions.text: A learner feels nervous before giving a report. Which is a healthy first step?
questions.explanation: Slow breathing and preparation can help manage nervousness.
questions.feedback: Slow breathing and preparation can help manage nervousness.

questions.text: What is one possible sign of stress?
questions.explanation: Stress can temporarily increase heart rate.
questions.feedback: Stress can temporarily increase heart rate.

questions.text: Which statement is assertive?
options: Do what I say or else
Please stop; that is not kind
questions.explanation: A clear and respectful request expresses a boundary.
questions.feedback: A clear and respectful request expresses a boundary.

questions.text: When should a learner seek a trusted adult's help?
options: When a situation feels unsafe or difficult to handle
questions.explanation: Trusted adults can provide support when needed.
questions.feedback: Trusted adults can provide support when needed.

questions.text: Which action shows positive self-talk?
options: I always fail so I quit
questions.explanation: Encouraging self-talk supports effort and coping.
questions.feedback: Encouraging self-talk supports effort and coping.

checkpoints.title: Field Play Yard
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Field Play Yard. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: In striking and fielding games, learners strike or send an object, move safely between spaces and try to prevent an opponent from scoring. Look for open space, stay aware of players, and follow the agreed rules. Movement skills include agility, balance and coordination.

miniGame.name: Field Placement
miniGame.instructions: Choose where to send the ball on a simple field diagram; move three markers to open spaces.

steps.prompt: In a striking game, where is the most effective and safe place to send the ball?
items: Directly into a crowded cluster of fielders
Toward open space away from defenders
Outside the play area boundary
steps.success: Spot on! Open space creates a scoring opportunity safely.

steps.prompt: Field Movement: sort these actions into Safe Play and Unsafe Play.
items: Looking around before running to avoid collisions
Pushing another player to reach the ball
Moving into a balanced ready position to field
Ignoring court boundaries and teammates
steps.success: Excellent sportsmanship and safety awareness!

questions.text: In a striking game, where is a useful place to send a ball?
options: Toward open space away from fielders
questions.explanation: Open space may give the striker an advantage without unsafe play.
questions.feedback: Open space may give the striker an advantage without unsafe play.

questions.text: Why is looking around before running important?
options: To notice teammates and avoid collisions
questions.explanation: Spatial awareness helps learners move safely.
questions.feedback: Spatial awareness helps learners move safely.

questions.text: Which skill helps a player change direction quickly?
questions.explanation: Agility is the ability to change direction efficiently.
questions.feedback: Agility is the ability to change direction efficiently.

questions.text: A fielder sees a ball approaching. What should the fielder do?
options: Move into a balanced ready position
Leave the play area without reason
questions.explanation: A ready position helps the player respond safely.
questions.feedback: A ready position helps the player respond safely.

questions.text: What shows sportsmanship?
questions.explanation: Respecting others and the rules is part of fair play.
questions.feedback: Respecting others and the rules is part of fair play.

checkpoints.title: Kindness Challenge Plaza
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Kindness Challenge Plaza. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Bullying can involve repeated harmful behavior and misuse of power. Learners can say no calmly when safe, support someone being hurt, and seek a trusted adult. During games, respect personal space, safety rules and different abilities.

miniGame.name: Decision Trail
miniGame.instructions: Choose responses at a bullying scenario and a teammate-safety scenario; each opens a different dialogue.

steps.prompt: A classmate is repeatedly teased during games. What is the most supportive action?
items: Cheer for the teasing and laugh along
Pretend nobody is affected and ignore it
Support the learner and tell a trusted adult
steps.success: Correct! Reporting bullying protects your classmates.

steps.prompt: Decision Trail: sort these statements into Assertive & Respectful vs Hurtful & Aggressive.
items: Please stop; that is not kind.
Do what I say or else!
I need personal space right now.
You always ruin our game!
steps.success: Great communication skills! Clear boundaries build a safe environment.

questions.text: Someone repeatedly makes fun of a learner during games. What should a witness do?
options: Support the learner and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Support and reporting can help stop repeated bullying.
questions.feedback: Support and reporting can help stop repeated bullying.

questions.text: Which response sets a safe boundary?
questions.explanation: Calm respectful words communicate a boundary.
questions.feedback: Calm respectful words communicate a boundary.

questions.text: A team is crowded on the left side of the field. Which tactic makes sense?
options: Move toward open space on the right
questions.explanation: Using open space supports effective movement in games.
questions.feedback: Using open space supports effective movement in games.

questions.text: A teammate struggles to catch a ball. What should others do?
options: Encourage and offer a safe practice chance
Throw the ball harder without warning
questions.explanation: Encouragement supports inclusion and skill development.
questions.feedback: Encouragement supports inclusion and skill development.

questions.text: Which plan supports both well-being and active play?
options: Quit every activity after an error
Use respectful words, ask for help, and follow game safety rules
questions.explanation: The plan combines healthy communication with safer participation.
questions.feedback: The plan combines healthy communication with safer participation.

missions.title: Growing Well, Playing Together
missions.story: Wellness Town opens a Growth & Play Festival. Learners learn to respect differences in growth, make supportive choices, and complete a net/wall game strategy challenge.
missions.focus: Puberty changes, healthy hygiene and trusted support; net/wall game skills, open-space tactics and teamwork.

finalChallenge.title: Festival Finale
finalChallenge.description: Festival final task: choose a supportive growth-related statement, select correct net/wall tactics and demonstrate a safe cooperative rally or movement pattern with teacher observation.

steps.prompt: A classmate expresses worry about growing at a different rate from others. What is the best response?
items: Growth timing differs naturally for everyone; you can always ask a trusted nurse or parent for guidance.
Everyone is supposed to grow identically at the exact same age.
You should avoid eating so you don't grow.
steps.success: Empathetic and accurate guidance!

steps.prompt: Net/Wall Strategy Challenge: classify each rally decision as Smart Tactic vs Ineffective Play.
items: Directing returns into uncovered spaces away from opponents
Hitting the ball blindly while looking away
Communicating clearly with your partner by calling 'Mine!'
Standing flat-footed without recovering court position
steps.success: Mission 2 complete! You earned the Growth and Teamwork Badge!

checkpoints.title: Growing Well Clinic
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Growing Well Clinic. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Puberty is a normal stage of development. Bodies and emotions change at different times and rates. Personal hygiene, adequate rest, balanced meals and trusted support can help. No one should be mocked for developing earlier or later.

miniGame.name: Myth or Fact
miniGame.instructions: Sort statements on changing height, body development and hygiene into fact or myth.

steps.prompt: Myth or Fact: sort each statement about puberty and growth changes.
items: Puberty is a normal stage of growth and timing varies for everyone
Every child must begin and finish puberty at the exact same age
Regular bathing and clean clothes support personal hygiene
Developing earlier or later means someone has an illness
steps.success: Well done! Understanding growth differences promotes respect and self-care.

questions.text: Which statement about puberty is accurate?
options: Every child changes at the exact same time
Puberty is normal and timing varies
questions.explanation: Puberty is part of growth and happens at different times.
questions.feedback: Puberty is part of growth and happens at different times.

questions.text: What is a helpful hygiene habit during puberty?
questions.explanation: Basic hygiene supports comfort and health.
questions.feedback: Basic hygiene supports comfort and health.

questions.text: A friend worries that they are growing later than classmates. What is kind advice?
options: Growth timing differs; speak with a trusted adult if concerned
questions.explanation: Variation is normal, and trusted adults can help with concerns.
questions.feedback: Variation is normal, and trusted adults can help with concerns.

questions.text: Which person may give reliable help about puberty questions?
options: A parent, guardian, nurse or health professional
A stranger selling a secret product
questions.explanation: Trusted adults and health professionals can give appropriate information.
questions.feedback: Trusted adults and health professionals can give appropriate information.

questions.text: Why should classmates avoid teasing about body changes?
options: It can harm feelings and respect
It changes the rate of growth
questions.explanation: Respect for differences supports emotional well-being.
questions.feedback: Respect for differences supports emotional well-being.

checkpoints.title: Net-Wall Court
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Net-Wall Court. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: In net/wall games, players send an object over a net or toward a wall, recover position and defend an area. Placing the object in open space can make return difficult. Learners should communicate, stay balanced and protect personal space.

miniGame.name: Target Zones
miniGame.instructions: Click an uncovered space on a simple court diagram; arrange receive, return and recover actions.

steps.prompt: Target Zones: tap the three key actions of a net/wall rally in the correct order.
items: Receive the ball in a balanced ready stance
Return the ball toward open space
Recover your position to defend the court
steps.success: Smooth rally technique! Receive, return, and recover.

steps.prompt: Where should a player usually aim to challenge the opposing team?
items: At an open space inside the court
Directly at the referee
Outside the court boundaries
steps.success: Great placement tactic!

questions.text: Where should a player usually aim to challenge an opponent?
options: At an open space inside the court
questions.explanation: Placing the object in an open legal area can be effective.
questions.feedback: Placing the object in an open legal area can be effective.

questions.text: After sending the ball over the net, what should the player do?
options: Sit in the middle of the court
questions.explanation: Returning to a ready position supports the next play.
questions.feedback: Returning to a ready position supports the next play.

questions.text: Which movement skill helps maintain control while receiving a ball?
questions.explanation: Balance helps control posture when receiving.
questions.feedback: Balance helps control posture when receiving.

questions.text: What does good team communication sound like?
options: Calling who will receive the ball
questions.explanation: Clear calls reduce confusion and collisions.
questions.feedback: Clear calls reduce confusion and collisions.

questions.text: Which choice supports safe net/wall participation?
options: Checking space and using controlled movements
questions.explanation: Awareness and control reduce injury risk.
questions.feedback: Awareness and control reduce injury risk.

checkpoints.title: Healthy Team Pavilion
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Healthy Team Pavilion. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: A supportive group respects different stages of growth and welcomes all learners into age-appropriate activity. Players can adapt tasks for varying abilities, communicate kindly and use hygiene routines after being active.

miniGame.name: Team Planner
miniGame.instructions: Select an inclusive game rule, a safe movement option and a post-play hygiene step.

steps.prompt: Team Planner: sort the habits into Inclusive & Healthy vs Unhealthy & Exclusive.
items: Give everyone an appropriate chance to participate
Let only expert players touch the ball
Wash and change into clean clothing after active play
Stay in sweaty, wet clothes all day
steps.success: Awesome! Inclusive teamwork and proper hygiene keep everyone healthy.

questions.text: A learner feels self-conscious about body changes. What is a helpful response?
options: Compare their body with everyone else's
questions.explanation: Respect and privacy create a supportive environment.
questions.feedback: Respect and privacy create a supportive environment.

questions.text: What is a healthy habit after a sweaty activity?
options: Keep wet clothing on all day
Wash and change into clean clothing
questions.explanation: Hygiene after activity supports health and comfort.
questions.feedback: Hygiene after activity supports health and comfort.

questions.text: A game has students with different skill levels. Which rule is most inclusive?
options: Give everyone an appropriate chance to participate
Let only experts touch the ball
questions.explanation: Fair participation supports learning for all players.
questions.feedback: Fair participation supports learning for all players.

questions.text: In a net/wall game, two teammates approach the same ball. What should help?
options: Calling clearly who will receive it
questions.explanation: Communication supports coordination and safety.
questions.feedback: Communication supports coordination and safety.

questions.text: What best combines health and PE learning?
options: Teasing others but winning the match
Respecting growth differences and playing safely
questions.explanation: Respectful conduct and safe movement support well-being.
questions.feedback: Respectful conduct and safe movement support well-being.

missions.title: Safe Choices, Active Rhythms
missions.story: The community is setting up a safe dance-and-games celebration. The learner must identify hazards, make responsible health choices and lead a simple rhythmic sequence.
missions.focus: Medicine safety, substance-risk decisions, road/activity injury prevention, rhythm/dance and safe participation.

finalChallenge.title: Festival Safety Finale
finalChallenge.description: Festival safety finale: identify four risks, choose a respectful refusal to an unsafe substance, and perform a safe movement sequence as feasible and teacher-observed.

steps.prompt: Festival Safety Finale: identify risks and safe choices.
items: Drinking water and resting between active dances
Taking prescription pills offered by an acquaintance
Stopping immediately and reporting when feeling sharp pain
Walking across a busy road while looking at a phone
steps.success: Safety precautions mastered!

steps.prompt: How should a learner assertively refuse an unsafe offer (like tobacco or unfamiliar pills)?
items: Accept it quietly so nobody gets upset
Say firmly and politely: 'No thank you, that is not safe for me,' and tell a trusted adult
Keep it in your pocket just in case
steps.success: Mission 3 complete! You earned the Active Safety Badge!

checkpoints.title: Safety and Choices Post
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Safety and Choices Post. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Medicines should be used only with guidance from a responsible adult and correct instructions. Never share or take unfamiliar medicine. Tobacco and alcohol can harm health, especially for children. Report hazards such as broken glass or damaged equipment.

miniGame.name: Safety Sort
miniGame.instructions: Sort household medicine, cigarettes, broken glass and safe first-aid supplies into seek-adult-help/report/avoid categories.

steps.prompt: Safety Sort: classify each item into Safe with Adult Guidance vs Hazard / Avoid & Report.
items: Prescription medicine taken with a parent or school nurse
Cigarettes and tobacco products
Broken glass on the playground path
Clean first-aid bandage used with adult help
steps.success: Great safety choices! Never take unfamiliar medicines or handle sharp hazards.

questions.text: A friend offers you medicine that was prescribed for another person. What should you do?
options: Refuse it and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Medicine for someone else should not be shared.
questions.feedback: Medicine for someone else should not be shared.

questions.text: What is the safest source of medicine-use instructions for a child?
options: A responsible adult following a health professional's directions
questions.explanation: Appropriate adult and professional guidance is important.
questions.feedback: Appropriate adult and professional guidance is important.

questions.text: Why should learners avoid tobacco?
options: It can harm health and cause dependence
questions.explanation: Tobacco use carries harmful health and dependence risks.
questions.feedback: Tobacco use carries harmful health and dependence risks.

questions.text: You see broken glass on a playground path. What should you do?
options: Stay clear and inform the teacher or caretaker
questions.explanation: Reporting and avoiding sharp hazards can prevent injury.
questions.feedback: Reporting and avoiding sharp hazards can prevent injury.

questions.text: Which medicine-related action is safe?
options: Following instructions with a responsible adult
Taking extra doses to improve quickly
questions.explanation: Use medicines with appropriate instruction and supervision.
questions.feedback: Use medicines with appropriate instruction and supervision.

checkpoints.title: Rhythm Circle
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Rhythm Circle. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Rhythmic activity uses beat, timing, direction, level and controlled movement. A simple three-beat practice counts ONE-two-three. Keep personal space and adjust movement to ability. PE also requires actual performance, not only clicking answers.

miniGame.name: Step Sequence
miniGame.instructions: Tap three beat icons in rhythm and arrange STEP–SIDE–CLOSE cards; use a quiet mode without audio if needed.

steps.prompt: Step Sequence: arrange the 3-beat rhythm sequence in order.
items: Count 1: Step forward
Count 2: Step to the side
Count 3: Close feet together
steps.success: Great rhythm and timing! ONE, two, three!

steps.prompt: Movement Levels: sort the dance actions by level.
items: Reaching overhead tall on tiptoes
Crouching safely toward the floor
Jumping with arms stretched high
Bending knees low near the floor
steps.success: Terrific movement coordination!

questions.text: How many counts are in a three-beat pattern?
questions.explanation: A three-beat pattern groups movements into three counts.
questions.feedback: A three-beat pattern groups movements into three counts.

questions.text: Which is a low-level movement?
questions.explanation: Crouching is performed at a lower level.
questions.feedback: Crouching is performed at a lower level.

questions.text: Why should a dancer keep enough personal space?
questions.explanation: Space allows people to move with less collision risk.
questions.feedback: Space allows people to move with less collision risk.

questions.text: Which action helps stay with a musical beat?
questions.explanation: Coordinating movement with the beat develops timing.
questions.feedback: Coordinating movement with the beat develops timing.

questions.text: If a learner loses the count, what is the best response?
options: Rejoin safely at the next count
questions.explanation: Calmly rejoining supports safe participation.
questions.feedback: Calmly rejoining supports safe participation.

checkpoints.title: Safe Journey Stage
checkpoints.npcOpening: Hello! Welcome to Safe Journey Stage. First read the lesson, then try our activity and answer the questions.
checkpoints.lesson: Before crossing a road, stop, look carefully, listen and cross only when it is safe and permitted. In physical activity, use suitable equipment, warm up, watch conditions and stop when injured. Safe movement and responsible choices support lifelong activity.

miniGame.name: Hazard Hunt
miniGame.instructions: Inspect a virtual road and dance area; mark slippery floor, damaged equipment and crossing risks.

steps.prompt: Hazard Hunt: tap the pedestrian road safety steps in the correct order.
items: Stop at the curb or sidewalk edge
Look left, right, and listen for traffic
Cross safely at the marked pedestrian lane
steps.success: Safe crossing routine mastered: Stop, Look, Listen, Cross!

steps.prompt: The stage floor is slippery before dance practice. What is the safest action?
items: Start dancing faster to dry it off
Report the hazard and wait until it is safe and clean
Challenge friends to slide on it
steps.success: Spot on! Reporting hazards prevents painful accidents.

questions.text: Where should a person cross a road whenever possible?
options: At a marked pedestrian crossing when safe
questions.explanation: A marked crossing helps pedestrians follow safer road practices.
questions.feedback: A marked crossing helps pedestrians follow safer road practices.

questions.text: Before stepping onto the road, what should a pedestrian do?
options: Use a phone and walk quickly
questions.explanation: Stopping and checking traffic helps assess risk.
questions.feedback: Stopping and checking traffic helps assess risk.

questions.text: Why should learners warm up before vigorous movement?
options: To prepare body and muscles for activity
questions.explanation: A suitable warm-up prepares the body for movement.
questions.feedback: A suitable warm-up prepares the body for movement.

questions.text: What should a dancer do if they feel sharp pain?
options: Stop and tell a teacher or coach
Ask a friend to pull the painful area
questions.explanation: Stopping and reporting pain can help prevent worsening injury.
questions.feedback: Stopping and reporting pain can help prevent worsening injury.

questions.text: A stage floor is slippery. What is the safest action?
options: Report the hazard and wait until it is safe
questions.explanation: Removing or avoiding a hazard is important before moving.
questions.feedback: Removing or avoiding a hazard is important before moving.
